name: Failed Lich
body:
FAILED LICH
CR 3

XP 800
CE Medium undead
Init -1; darkvision 60 ft.; Perception +9

DEFENSE

AC 11, touch 9, flat-footed 11 (-1 Dex, +2 natural)
hp 36 (4d6 + 22)
Fort +1, Ref +0, Will +8
Defensive Abilities +2 turn resistance; DR 5/slashing; Immune undead traits

OFFENSE

Speed 30 ft.
Melee slam +3 (1d6+1), touch +3 (by spell)
Ranged dart +1 (1d4+1)
Space 5 ft.; Reach 5 ft.
Special Attacks grave touch (1d6 cold plus shaken), command undead
Spells Prepared (CL 4th; concentration +6)

2nd—ghoul touch (DC 14), scare (DC 14), spectral hand
1st—cause fear (DC 13), chill touch (2, DC 13), ray of enfeeblement (DC 13)
0 (at will)—acid splash, mage hand, read magic, touch of fatigue (DC 12)

STATISTICS

Str 13, Dex 8, Con —, Int 14, Wis 15, Cha 16
Base Atk +2; CMB +3; CMD 12
Feats Toughness, Craft Wondrous Item, Weapon Focus (Touch)
Skills Appraise +9, Craft (alchemy) +7, Knowledge (arcana) +9, Knowledge (history) +9, Linguistics +9, Profession (hotelier) +7, Spellcraft +9
Languages Common, Infernal, Abyssal
SQ staggered, +2 turn resistance
Combat Gear Rat Skull Talisman (casts scare 1/day), Robe of the Glowing Arcana (casts mage armor)

ABOUT

The failed lich was once an eccentric book trader and manor proprietor who sought the eternal power and majesty of lichdom. Impatient and lacking the profound arcane mastery required to craft a true phylactery, he conducted a flawed ritual that transformed him into an intelligent, spellcasting zombie.

Trapped in delusional madness, he genuinely believes his ascension was a complete success. He holds court in his subterranean laboratory surrounded by dissected cadavers and bubbling cauldrons, commanding legions of stitched and unsewn undead.

In battle, he casts spectral hand to deliver paralyzing ghoul touch and strength-draining rays from behind a defensive shield of raised thralls, retreating only when his skeletal body is shattered.

True lichdom requires profound discipline, vast wealth, and legendary arcane fortitude. When arrogant necromancers attempt shortcuts or use counterfeit formulae, the resulting ritual curses their physical form, rotting away their flesh while trapping their intellect inside a decaying carcass.

The tragedy of the Failed Lich is their total detachment from reality: they guard false phylacteries that hold no soul and issue grandiose decrees to shambling minions, entirely oblivious that they have become the very abominations they once commanded.
